source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
For growing corn, farmers should select land that meets the following conditions: soil that drains water well and does not retain standing water; soil with abundant organic matter, a pH of about 6 to 7; soil that is free of rock/gravel and is not sandy; and soil that is not eroded/degraded.

In Cambodia, land types considered suitable for corn are: riverbank land (along rivers/streams), levee/dyke land, land along canals, land in upland (chamkar) fields, and reddish basalt soil (ដីក្រហម).

Benefits of good land selection: choosing land with these qualities lets the corn root system spread and take up nutrients efficiently within the soil and lets the plant stand firmly against wind. It also allows the roots to fully absorb nutrients left over from prior crop residue and soil amendments, which improves the health of the following crop and increases the fertility level of the field over time, since good soil quality can accumulate nutrients from repeated seasons and reduce the need to buy additional fertilizer, while erosion control and appropriate liming and drainage measures further help sustain productivity.
